title: SLO Notifications Playbook + Wireframes (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
Quick working playbook + wireframe notes for SLO/Alert/Notification UX in Console. Goal is to converge on an MVP surface that covers: per-route SLOs, multi-channel routing, threshold templates, and operator-friendly policy management (mute, snooze, group). This is a working board — lots of ‘todo’ & questions inline.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Console UX for configuring SLOs and alert policies (not the infra routing implementation).
- Notification channels: Slack, Email, PagerDuty (PD), Webhook, Console banner, Mobile push.
- Policy primitives: threshold, rolling window, aggregation (per-route / per-model / customer), severity, suppression rules, escalation.
- Wireframe notes for configuration page + incident drawer + alert inbox.

Primary personas:
- Platform engineer (creates org-wide baseline SLOs and escalation paths)
- Product engineer (configures per-route SLOs for their feature)
- On-call responder (needs clear context + quick runbook links)
- Manager (wants weekly digest and SLA exposures)

Design goals / constraints:
- Make common tasks 1–2 clicks (enable default SLO, turn on Slack channel).
- Defaults are opinionated but editable: we provide reasonable templates for latency and error-rate SLOs per model class.
- Support multi-tenant orgs: scoping (org / workspace / project) must be explicit on the top of the page.
- Minimize cognitive load: group similar alert triggers into one aggregated notification by default.

High-level pages / flows (wireframe sketch in text):
1) Monitoring -> SLOs (list view)
   - Left: filters (team, model, route, region, status).
   - Center: table of SLOs (name, target, current burn rate, status badge, last alert).
   - Right: quick actions: Edit, View Incidents, Duplicate, Disable.
   - Inline: 'Enable default alerts' toggle to auto-create a basic policy for this SLO.

2) SLO Detail / Policy Editor (3-column modal)
   - Column A (left): SLO summary + graph (rolling window p50/p95/p99, error rate) + last 14 days.
   - Column B (middle): Policy builder (list of rules):
       * Rule: metric (latency/error/availability), aggregator (p95/p99/avg), threshold, window (5m/15m/1h/24h), severity.
       * UI: add rule -> pick template -> adjust numeric threshold -> simulate impact (estimate alerts/day based on last 14d).
   - Column C (right): Notification routing and actions:
       * Channels (checkbox list): Slack channel selector, Email list, PagerDuty service, webhook url, console banner.
       * Escalation chain: primary -> after X minutes escalate to secondary -> after Y minutes notify manager.
       * Snooze & suppression rules: ad-hoc snooze, scheduled maintenance windows, auto-suppress during rollouts.

3) Incident drawer (appears when alert clicked)
   - Top summary: why fired, related SLO, severity, time, aging.
   - Context tabs: Recent requests (sample logs), last deployment id, config snapshot, runbook link, playbook notes.
   - Actions: Acknowledge, Add note, Re-route to PD, Run rollback (link to deploy console).

Notification channel routing: mapping ideas:
- Default routing per team: map slack channel + PD service + email group.
- Per-policy overrides possible for critical SLOs.
- Channel templates: quick pick list (e.g., 'On-call (primary)', 'Ops-corridor', 'PagerDuty-critical').
- Webhook: allow variable substitution in payload ({{slo_name}}, {{status}}, {{current_value}}, {{link}}).

Threshold & policy examples (to be used as templates):
- Latency SLO (generation): target p95 < 200ms over 30d, alert rule: p95 > 300ms for 15m (severity: high).
- Availability SLO (API route): target 99.9% over 30d, alert rule: error_rate > 0.5% for 5m (severity: critical).
- Cost/Performance policy: token_cost_per_request > $0.10 for 1h (notify finance & owner).
- Burn-rate style: ratio of error_budget_spent > 1.0 in 1h (severity: critical -> trigger org-wide banner).

Aggregation & noise reduction rules (defaults):
- Group by route+region for first alert, then collapse repeated alerts into a single incident until recovery or new root cause.
- Suppress low-severity alerts if a higher severity alert for same route is active.
- Auto-snooze alerts during detected deployments (if deploy tag present) with opt-out.

Escalation & TTL:
- Acknowledge window: 15 minutes for severity=critical before escalation.
- Escalation step intervals: 15m, 30m.
- Auto-resolve rules: auto-resolve if metric returns under threshold for 2x the triggering window.

Backlog grooming notes (tickets & acceptance criteria):
- PROJ-7812: SLO list + filters (priority P0)
  - AC: list view shows SLO name, target, current burn, last alert; filter by team; row actions Edit/View/Disable.
- PROJ-7813: Policy builder MVP (priority P0)
  - AC: user can add rule, set metric/aggregator/threshold/window, save policy, simulation shows estimated alerts/day.
- PROJ-7814: Notification channel integration (P1)
  - AC: connect Slack workspace + select channel; select PagerDuty service; save routing.
- PROJ-7815: Incident drawer + context (P1)
  - AC: show runbook link, last deploy id, sample request logs (first 5 rows), ability to acknowledge.
- PROJ-7820: Aggregation & suppression heuristics (P2)
  - AC: duplicate alerts for same route within 5m are grouped into a single incident.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Simulated alert frequency: should we surface an estimate based on historical data by default? (pros: helps set thresholds; cons: needs infra compute).
- Who can create global escalation policies? Org admins only? Platform team?
- Template library: provide model-class-based defaults (e.g., chat-generation vs embeddings). Need SME input from Applied ML.
- How do we represent multi-model routes where a route can be served by multiple variants? (policy should allow tag-based scoping).

Small UI interaction notes (usability):
- When editing numeric threshold, display live impact bar showing % change in estimated alerts.
- Provide one-click 'Apply to siblings' (apply policy to all routes under same model).
- 'Mute for release' quick action available on SLO list row with dropdown for 30m/1h/4h.
- Export incidents to CSV and attach to weekly SLO report.

Temporary UX experiments to try (A/B ideas):
- A: Show alerts/day simulation in policy editor. B: Hide simulation but show historical metric overlay for last 7d. Measure configuration time & threshold tuning accuracy.
- A: Default grouping by route+region. B: Default grouping by root-cause fingerprint (requires fingerprinting service).

Next steps / action items:
- Design: create high-fidelity mockups for SLO list + policy editor (Ethan) — due 2025-11-28.
- Eng: spike for simulation API (Marcel) — determine cost & lat for historical scan by 2025-11-24.
- Applied ML: recommend default SLO templates for model classes (Lena) — deliver suggestions 2025-11-21.
- PM: finalize open decisions and ownership for global escalation policies (Priya) — meeting 2025-11-07.

Notes to self: keep the first iteration small — per-policy routing + default templates + incident drawer cover 80% of needs. Defer fancy fingerprint grouping and complex ML-based suppression to phase 2.

Unresolved UX language: what do we call "SLO policy" vs "Alert rule"? My current thought: SLO = long-running objective; Policy = a named set of Alert Rules + Routing + Escalation bound to an SLO.

End of draft.
